theme: It is good to give thanks to the LORD, the Sabbath psalm
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 92. It is the only psalm in the Psalter that is labeled “A Song for the Sabbath Day,” and it ends this unit with praise. Read it slowly, and let it be a song of gratitude for everything you have read.
settingTheScene: Psalm 92 is a song for the Sabbath. It was sung in the worship of Israel on the weekly day of rest. It is a psalm of thanksgiving that celebrates God’s works and contrasts the end of the wicked with the flourishing of the righteous. It is a fitting close to a unit about God’s dwelling with his people, because the picture at the end is of the righteous planted in the house of the LORD.
observation: “It is good to give thanks to the LORD, to sing praises to your name, O Most High” (v. 1).
The praise is “to declare your steadfast love in the morning, and your faithfulness by night” (v. 2).
“For you, O LORD, have made me glad by your work; at the works of your hands I sing for joy” (v. 4).
“How great are your works, O LORD! Your thoughts are very deep!” (v. 5).
“The stupid man cannot know; the fool cannot understand this: that though the wicked sprout like grass and all evildoers flourish, they are doomed to destruction forever” (vv. 6-7).
“But you, O LORD, are on high forever” (v. 8).
“The righteous flourish like the palm tree and grow like a cedar in Lebanon” (v. 12).

“They are planted in the house of the LORD; they flourish in the courts of our God. They still bear fruit in old age; they are ever full of sap and green, to declare that the LORD is upright” (vv. 13-15).
interpretation:
The psalm begins with a simple statement, “It is good to give thanks to the LORD.” Giving thanks is not a duty to be endured. It is good, a pleasure and a benefit. The psalm describes a day of rest filled with song and gratitude, with the harp and the lyre, morning and night.

The Sabbath is a day for remembering that God is the maker and doer. “You, O LORD, have made me glad by your work.” It is the work of God that makes the psalmist glad, not his own. The Sabbath is a day of rest because Israel’s life depends on what God has done. It is a weekly declaration that salvation is grace.

The middle of the psalm looks at the wicked. They may flourish for a time, “like grass,” but the grass withers. The psalmist wants us to see that apparent success is short-lived, and that God’s reign endures. “You, O LORD, are on high forever.” This is the steady center of the song.

The final image is one of the most beautiful in the Psalms. The righteous are like trees, a palm and a cedar, planted in the house of the LORD. A tree planted in a temple courtyard is sheltered, watered, and fed. And it keeps bearing fruit, even in old age. The picture is of a long, fruitful life lived near God.

This connects to the tabernacle. The tabernacle was filled with garden images, a lampstand shaped like a tree and curtains woven with fruit, because God’s dwelling place is the place where life flourishes. The psalm shows what happens to someone who is planted there. He grows. He does not dry up. And he lives to declare that the LORD is upright.
connection: Jesus said, “The Sabbath was made for man” (Mark 2:27), and that he is “lord of the Sabbath.” He is also the vine in whom believers abide and bear much fruit (John 15:5). Psalm 1 describes the same flourishing tree. Paul says that believers are “filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ” (Philippians 1:11). Hebrews 4 promises a Sabbath rest for the people of God. And Revelation 22:2 describes the tree of life in the new Jerusalem, whose leaves are “for the healing of the nations.”
application:
Give thanks aloud for three works of God you have seen this week. Name them specifically.

Think about where you are planted. Are you connected to a local church, so that you can grow in the courts of the LORD?

Ask God to make you a person who keeps bearing fruit, even into old age.
prayerPrompts: Give thanks to God for his work in you, in your own words.
Ask him to plant you in his house and keep you fruitful.
Tell him that he is upright and faithful.
